+# Authenticated paired HTTP token rotation — DPA-v1
+
+Status: implementation contract; exact-H Actions and external acceptance pending.
+Task: `647e0932-bea4-4113-9a61-65ae3db58955`, round 1.
+Fixed U: `1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845`, tree
+`90c8aab39972da11cfad220361781d49e1bc6700`.
+Discovery target: tree `15911945f31b8a11b7d32e0072110ff3a75c18e4`;
+current integration base `f71bb36a8757b4acf2356fa34de9d73721ccfbda`, tree
+`094035e3c9121ad75f85b4dfb35594c3bbb2b2e8`. The pairing owner remains blob
+`510d42d62acc1a0a0b95a651f343bbb9bcc5690d`; intervening App changes belong to
+MCP/channel processing. Integrate after the reviewed DPR-v1 CI consolidation.
+
+## Problem and existing ownership
+
+The HTTP server authenticates a paired bearer, but drops its identity at the
+generic command boundary. The rotation owner receives only target arguments.
+An ordinary operator/write caller can therefore address another device and
+obtain its replacement token by omitting `crossDevice`. An explicit failed
+bearer on a listener with no configured secret can fall back to ambient native
+authority. Separately, the authentication snapshot has no binding to the token
+generation actually presented, so replacement/revocation before mutation is
+not rechecked. These are source findings, not an executed exploit report.
+
+The single production chain remains HTTP Gateway → `UnifiedGatewayApi` →
+`DevicePairingOwner` → its existing SQLite pairing/token/revision tables →
+commit → the existing Gateway response/report path. This batch extends that
+owner and its typed Rust boundary. It introduces no store, permission service,
+schema migration, scheduler, Agent loop or frontend policy.
+
+## Shared Rust contract
+
+`DeviceTokenAuthorization` keeps its public device/role/scopes projection and
+adds a private, cloneable owner-issued proof. Only authentication's same locked
+token comparison may issue it. It seals the issuer allocation, device ID, role,
+accepted token SHA-256 and admitted scopes. Public projection mutations cannot
+change the sealed principal/grant. No serde/public proof constructor or raw
+bearer in context/debug/errors is allowed. Proof debug output is redacted;
+issuer equality uses allocation identity, not unit-value equality. Reopening
+an owner preserves persisted tokens but requires newly issued proofs.
+
+The existing owner exposes
+`rotate_token_for_authenticated_device(&self, args: &Value, authorization:
+&DeviceTokenAuthorization, scope_ceiling: Option<&str>)` returning the existing
+`Result<Value, GatewayCommandError>`. The optional string is the singular
+`x-sand-scope` ceiling; it can only constrain authority.
+
+`GatewayApi::rotate_paired_device_token(&self, args: Value, authorization:
+&DeviceTokenAuthorization, scope_ceiling: Option<&str>, context:
+&GatewayCommandContext)` has the same result type and a fail-closed default.
+Recognized paired HTTP rotation invokes this hook instead of the generic
+dispatch. The actual App override delegates to the same pairing owner and
+performs the same single desktop-contact update as normal `call`. The hook
+result joins the existing timing/report/error/response path. Native direct and
+configured-secret calls keep their existing dispatcher. Other Gateway methods
+and the generic context contract are unchanged.
+
+## Required behavior and observable oracles
+
+| ID | Contract |
+| --- | --- |
+| DPA-01 | Recognized paired rotation always carries its sealed credential into the bound hook. The default hook refuses instead of falling back to legacy `call`. An explicit invalid/blank/malformed/retired bearer cannot become native on a secret-free listener. Credential-absent native mode requires the actual listener to be loopback, not just a loopback Host header. Configured native-secret and intended public pairing request/status behavior remain. |
+| DPA-02 | Begin an immediate SQLite write transaction while holding the existing owner mutex before reading caller or target facts. Re-admit the exact issuer/device/role/token fingerprint and current approved role/baseline. The entire live token grant must still fit the current approved baseline; a partly unapproved live token cannot retain a smaller permission subset. Missing/replaced/revoked or no-longer-approved credentials refuse with 401. A different owner or mutated public projection cannot manufacture proof. No unlocked precheck followed by a separate mutation is sufficient. |
+| DPA-03 | The caller must currently be an operator with the existing rotation write permission. For each requested permission, all of the sealed admitted grant, live token grant, current approval ceiling and optional header ceiling must allow it. Admin implies operator permissions; write implies only read/talk/cron/sessions.read/sessions.write, and read or sessions.write implies sessions.read. Non-operator scopes require their own role prefix and literal membership. Unknown roles, forged headers/body caller fields and blank ceilings cannot grant authority. |
+| DPA-04 | Non-admin callers may manage only their own operator token. Check cross-device/non-operator-role authority before revealing target state. Admin may rotate another approved device/role, bounded by that target's approval. No header can supply missing admin; a write ceiling on an admin bearer removes cross-device authority. |
+| DPA-05 | Target role defaults to operator; paired request types must be valid. Desired scopes come from explicit scopes (including an explicit empty array), otherwise the existing role token scopes, otherwise the target's role-filtered baseline. Prefer approved_scopes_json, fall back to scopes_json only when SQL NULL; missing/malformed data refuses without a permissive default. Require desired scopes within the target baseline and, for operator tokens, every caller ceiling. Reject unauthorized requested scopes rather than silently discarding them. Omission must not expand a narrower existing token to the whole baseline. |
+| DPA-06 | After all checks, generate one token, replace only the selected entry, clear the same retained/pending node surfaces, advance revision using DPR-v1, check one affected row, and commit before success. Any parse/policy/RNG/SQL/revision/commit error returns no successful receipt or secret. Preserve other role tokens and atomic rollback. |
+| DPA-07 | Paired in-band delivery derives only from sealed caller ID == target ID. Body crossDevice/caller/admin fields cannot change permission or disclosure. Self receives the committed token even with crossDevice=true; authorized cross-device admin receives withheld-cross-device and no token. Native crossDevice semantics, method name, default role, token prefix and response fields remain compatible. |
+| DPA-08 | If caller retirement commits before bound admission, a paused HTTP request refuses; if rotation commits first, later retirement does not retroactively undo it. Concurrent self-rotations with one original credential admit exactly one replacement. Unrelated device revision changes do not retire a current caller. Refusal/replacement and unaffected-role authority survive reopen. Never automatically replay a lost/unknown result. |
+
+Malformed request arguments use 400, denied grants use 403, retired/untrusted
+credentials use 401, and corrupt stored authorization or storage failure uses
+the existing internal-error boundary. New diagnostics exclude token bytes,
+fingerprints and raw persisted JSON. Authentication-only provenance remains
+distinct from an always-current grant; the definitive checks are inside the
+mutation transaction. Native rotation reuses the same transaction/update code
+without being silently converted into a paired principal.
+
+## Implementation and validation campaign
+
+Root integrates the owner/proof, public trait, actual App composition, workflow
+and RTM serially. Test workers may own disjoint new owner and HTTP contract
+files against this DPA-v1 contract and an exact base; they do not modify the
+shared public files. Replace the sole synthetic authorization struct literal
+in the old Gateway fixture with an actually issued owner credential.
+
+Use a real file-backed owner and independently opened read-only SQLite
+observations of both devices, token maps, roles/scopes/baselines, surfaces,
+pending rows and raw revision type/value/timestamp. Observe old/new token
+authentication, unchanged nonselected roles and reopen behavior. Cover self,
+cross-device, node/admin/write/read/unknown-role, header reduction/forgery,
+explicit/omitted/empty/implied scopes, corrupt/missing approval, revision
+corruption/exhaustion, foreign-owner proof and altered public projection.
+
+HTTP controls use `start_gateway_server` and actual TCP/HTTP with a thin API
+delegate to the production owner, no copied policy. A barrier in that delegate
+pauses after real authentication, then production token replacement/removal
+retires the caller before dispatch resumes. Compare the target/revision to the
+state after that independent retirement. Include positive no-retirement and
+two-concurrent-self controls with bounded waits, not scheduling sleeps. Test
+the fail-closed trait default and native/public controls. Existing real App
+compilation plus a bounded wiring check covers the shipping override; a thin
+test adapter is not described as a full shipping-binary runtime test.
+
+Freeze the complete candidate and obtain independent security/lifetime and
+structure/reuse/performance review. Run affected Host/App compilation, both
+new complete contract targets and preserved DPR/DPS/Gateway/Memory controls in
+the existing GitHub Actions lanes. Receipts bind exact H/tree/U, source and log
+hashes, zero command/capture exits and all named positive tests with no ignored
+or failed cases. No local/htch executable validation. A source approval or old
+H result cannot satisfy this candidate's behavior evidence.
+
+## Source, release and remaining scope
+
+Necessary fixed-U sources: devices.ts blob
+`532afea705ba73a2ff38a99043eadee4f9f6af60`, device-management-authz.ts
+`6d4e874d6a6cb97ce46e54103533a436ec93c471`, device-pairing-tokens.kernel.ts
+`5c61ce1a12a816dd5c147a91f66a0f1f837051d4`, device-pairing-token-policy.ts
+`36b7e7da9ee177b31fad17e379743418c558a18f`, operator-scope-compat.ts
+`a265fb895a8535378e9bb9626c19a030df463e1f`, device-pairing-identity.ts
+`cba1da2c85a9955b5793acefc70d86b5c3bc68cf`, and the DPR transaction/store
+source. The assessment records actual dependency read extent separately;
+historical OCRM reading facts and global flags are not promoted.
+
+No database conversion, reset or new persisted permission field is needed.
+Existing records retain their tokens; paired rotation now refuses unauthorized
+or corrupt requests. Rolling back source restores the known authorization
+defect, so rollback needs an explicit operational choice. Existing Gateway
+diagnostics/reporting carry refusals, without logging secrets.
+
+This closes only the declared paired HTTP rotation contract. U aliases,
+shared-auth token-delivery parity, other pairing management authorization,
+websocket invalidation, external token import/resurrection, issuer-generation
+policy, worker/device teardown, arbitrary database replacement, full companion
+devices/platform packages and actual release/upgrade/rollback/soak remain
+required subsequent scope. Native whole-device revoke keeps its meaning. No
+claim of isolation across every pairing method, physical-device acceptance,
+complete source closure, G01–G12, AC01–AC24 or independent final ACCEPT follows.

+//! Spec: projects/openclaw-rust/docs/specs/device-pairing-authenticated-rotation.md.
+//! Fixed U: 1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845.
+//! The scope cases below are explicit oracle examples from U's
+//! src/shared/operator-scope-compat.ts, not a second implementation of its policy.
+//! These tests make no HTTP, shipping-binary, or physical-device acceptance claim.
+

+const CALLER: &str = "dpa-device-a";
+const TARGET: &str = "dpa-device-b";
+const REVISION_KEY: &str = "devicePairing.revision";
+type StoredRow = BTreeMap<String, SqlValue>;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+struct StoredState {
+    paired: Vec<StoredRow>,
+    pending: Vec<StoredRow>,
+    revision: Vec<StoredRow>,
+}
+
+fn read_rows(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> Vec<StoredRow> {
+    let mut statement = conn.prepare(sql).expect("prepare independent SQL observation");
+    let columns: Vec<String> = statement.column_names().into_iter().map(str::to_owned).collect();
+    let rows = statement
+        .query_map([], |row| {
+            columns
+                .iter()
+                .enumerate()
+                .map(|(index, column)| Ok((column.clone(), row.get::<_, SqlValue>(index)?)))
+                .collect::<rusqlite::Result<StoredRow>>()
+        })
+        .expect("query complete fixture rows")
+        .collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()
+        .expect("retain each raw SQL value");
+    rows
+}
+
+fn text<'a>(row: &'a StoredRow, column: &str) -> &'a str {
+    match row.get(column) {
+        Some(SqlValue::Text(value)) => value,
+        _ => panic!("expected SQL TEXT in {column}"),
+    }
+}
+
+fn paired<'a>(state: &'a StoredState, device: &str) -> &'a StoredRow {
+    let matches: Vec<_> = state.paired.iter().filter(|row| text(row, "device_id") == device).collect();
+    assert_eq!(matches.len(), 1, "exactly one paired fixture device");
+    matches[0]
+}
+
+fn tokens(state: &StoredState, device: &str) -> Value {
+    serde_json::from_str(text(paired(state, device), "tokens_json"))
+        .expect("decode independently observed token map")
+}
+
+fn token(state: &StoredState, device: &str, role: &str) -> String {
+    tokens(state, device)[role]["token"].as_str().expect("persisted fixture token").to_owned()
+}
+
+fn revision(state: &StoredState) -> u64 {
+    assert_eq!(state.revision.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(text(&state.revision[0], "sql_type"), "text");
+    text(&state.revision[0], "value_json").trim_matches('"').parse().expect("known valid counter")
+}
+
+fn assert_revision(state: &StoredState, expected: u64) {
+    assert_eq!(state.revision.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(text(&state.revision[0], "state_key"), REVISION_KEY);
+    assert_eq!(text(&state.revision[0], "sql_type"), "text");
+    assert_eq!(text(&state.revision[0], "value_json"), format!("\"{expected}\""));
+    assert!(matches!(state.revision[0].get("updated_at_ms"), Some(SqlValue::Integer(value)) if *value > 0));
+}
+
+fn assert_scopes(actual: &Value, expected: &[&str]) {
+    let actual: Vec<_> = actual.as_array().expect("scope array").iter()
+        .map(|value| value.as_str().expect("string scope")).collect();
+    assert_eq!(actual.len(), expected.len(), "no silently discarded or additional scopes");
+    assert_eq!(actual.into_iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>(), expected.iter().copied().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>());
+}

+        assert!(matches!(column, "role" | "roles_json" | "scopes_json" | "approved_scopes_json" | "tokens_json"));

+fn assert_rotation(
+    fixture: &Fixture,
+    before: &StoredState,
+    receipt: &Value,
+    target: &str,
+    role: &str,
+    expected_scopes: &[&str],
+    in_band: bool,
+) -> String {
+    let after = fixture.observe();
+    let expected_revision = revision(before).checked_add(1).expect("successful fixture has counter headroom");
+    assert_eq!(receipt["revision"].as_u64(), Some(expected_revision));
+    assert_revision(&after, expected_revision);
+    assert_eq!(receipt["deviceId"], target);
+    assert_eq!(receipt["role"], role);
+    assert_eq!(after.pending, before.pending, "all pending rows and their timestamps survive rotation");
+    assert_eq!(after.paired.len(), before.paired.len());
+
+    for prior in &before.paired {
+        let device = text(prior, "device_id");
+        let current = paired(&after, device);
+        if device != target {
+            assert_eq!(current, prior, "the other complete paired row must be unchanged");
+        } else {
+            for (column, value) in prior {
+                if !matches!(column.as_str(), "tokens_json" | "node_surface_json" | "pending_node_surface_json") {
+                    assert_eq!(current.get(column), Some(value), "rotation changed unrelated column {column}");
+                }
+            }
+            assert_eq!(current.get("node_surface_json"), Some(&SqlValue::Null));
+            assert_eq!(current.get("pending_node_surface_json"), Some(&SqlValue::Null));
+        }
+    }
+
+    let prior_entries = tokens(before, target);
+    let current_entries = tokens(&after, target);
+    let new_bearer = current_entries[role]["token"].as_str().expect("committed replacement token").to_owned();
+    let mut expected_entries = prior_entries.clone();
+    expected_entries[role] = current_entries[role].clone();
+    assert_eq!(current_entries, expected_entries, "only the selected role entry may change");
+    assert_eq!(current_entries[role]["role"], role);
+    assert_scopes(&current_entries[role]["scopes"], expected_scopes);
+    assert_eq!(current_entries[role]["rotatedAtMs"], receipt["rotatedAtMs"]);
+    assert_eq!(current_entries[role]["createdAtMs"], receipt["rotatedAtMs"]);
+    assert!(current_entries[role].get("revokedAtMs")
+        .is_none_or(|value| value.is_null() || value.as_i64() == Some(0)));
+    assert!(receipt["rotatedAtMs"].as_i64().is_some_and(|value| value > 0));
+    let payload = new_bearer.strip_prefix("sand-device-tok-").expect("unchanged native token prefix");
+    assert_eq!(base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.decode(payload).expect("base64url token").len(), 32);
+    if let Some(old_bearer) = prior_entries[role]["token"].as_str() {
+        assert_ne!(new_bearer, old_bearer);
+        assert_invalid(fixture, old_bearer);
+    }
+    if in_band {
+        assert_eq!(receipt["tokenDelivery"], "in-band");
+        assert_eq!(receipt["token"].as_str(), Some(new_bearer.as_str()));
+    } else {
+        assert_eq!(receipt["tokenDelivery"], "withheld-cross-device");
+        assert!(receipt.get("token").is_none());
+        assert!(!receipt.to_string().contains(&new_bearer), "cross-device response leaks committed token");
+    }
+    fixture.issued_tokens.borrow_mut().push(new_bearer.clone());
+    assert_authorized(fixture, &new_bearer, target, role, expected_scopes);
+    for prior in &before.paired {
+        let device = text(prior, "device_id");
+        let entries = tokens(before, device);
+        for (entry_role, entry) in entries.as_object().expect("prior role map") {
+            if device == target && entry_role == role {
+                continue;
+            }
+            let scopes: Vec<_> = entry["scopes"].as_array().expect("unchanged scope array").iter()
+                .map(|value| value.as_str().expect("unchanged string scope")).collect();
+            assert_authorized(fixture, entry["token"].as_str().expect("unchanged bearer"), device, entry_role, &scopes);
+        }
+    }
+    new_bearer

+    let third = assert_rotation(&fixture, &before, &receipt, CALLER, "operator", &["operator.write"], true);
+
+    let captured = fixture.authorize_token(&third);
+    let before = fixture.observe();
+    let removed_node = token(&before, CALLER, "node");
+    let revoke = fixture.owner().handle_pairing_command(
+        "device.pair.revoke", &json!({"deviceId": CALLER}),
+    ).expect("existing native whole-device revoke retires every role");
+    let retired = fixture.observe();
+    assert_eq!(revoke["revision"].as_u64(), Some(revision(&before) + 1));
+    assert_revision(&retired, revision(&before) + 1);
+    assert_eq!(retired.pending, before.pending);
+    assert_eq!(retired.paired.len(), before.paired.len() - 1);
+    assert_eq!(paired(&retired, TARGET), paired(&before, TARGET));
+    assert!(!retired.paired.iter().any(|row| text(row, "device_id") == CALLER));
+    fixture.refuse(&captured, json!({"deviceId": CALLER}), None, 401);
+    assert_invalid(&fixture, &third);
+    assert_invalid(&fixture, &removed_node);
+    fixture.reopen();

+    fixture.refuse(&captured, json!({"deviceId": CALLER}), None, 401);
+    assert_invalid(&fixture, &third);
+    assert_invalid(&fixture, &removed_node);
+    let unaffected = fixture.authorization(TARGET, "operator");
+    let before = fixture.observe();
+    let receipt = fixture.owner().rotate_token_for_authenticated_device(
+        &json!({"deviceId": TARGET}), &unaffected, None,
+    ).expect("the other device's durable authority remains usable after revoke and reopen");
+    assert_rotation(&fixture, &before, &receipt, TARGET, "operator", &["operator.write"], true);
+
+    for retirement in ["missing-token", "revoked-entry", "unapproved-role"] {
+        let fixture = Fixture::seeded(retirement, &["operator.write"], &["operator.write"]);
+        let proof = fixture.authorization(CALLER, "operator");
+        match retirement {
+            "missing-token" => fixture.remove_role_token(CALLER, "operator"),
+            "revoked-entry" => {
+                let mut entries = tokens(&fixture.observe(), CALLER);
+                entries["operator"]["revokedAtMs"] = json!(1234);
+                fixture.write_column(CALLER, "tokens_json", &SqlValue::Text(entries.to_string()));
+            }
+            "unapproved-role" => {
+                fixture.write_column(CALLER, "role", &SqlValue::Text("node".to_owned()));
+                fixture.write_column(CALLER, "roles_json", &SqlValue::Text("[\"node\"]".to_owned()));
+            }
+            _ => unreachable!(),
+        }
+        fixture.refuse(&proof, json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "scopes": ["operator.write"]}), None, 401);
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn paired_rotation_admin_other_roles_require_literal_prefixed_baseline() {
+    let fixture = Fixture::seeded("admin-node", &["operator.admin"], &["operator.write", "node.read", "node.write"]);
+    let proof = fixture.authorization(CALLER, "operator");
+    let before = fixture.observe();
+    let receipt = fixture.owner().rotate_token_for_authenticated_device(
+        &json!({"deviceId": TARGET, "role": "node", "scopes": ["node.read"], "crossDevice": false}),
+        &proof, None,
+    ).expect("real operator admin can manage a different approved node role within its literal baseline");
+    assert_rotation(&fixture, &before, &receipt, TARGET, "node", &["node.read"], false);
+    let before = fixture.observe();
+    let receipt = fixture.owner().rotate_token_for_authenticated_device(
+        &json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "role": "node", "scopes": ["node.invoke"], "crossDevice": true}),
+        &proof, None,
+    ).expect("admin self-node rotation delivers in band based on sealed device identity");
+    assert_rotation(&fixture, &before, &receipt, CALLER, "node", &["node.invoke"], true);
+    fixture.refuse(&proof, json!({"deviceId": TARGET, "role": "unapproved-role", "scopes": []}), None, 403);
+
+    let node_cases: &[(&str, &[&str], &[&str])] = &[
+        ("node-no-write-implication", &["node.write"], &["node.read"]),
+        ("node-no-prefix-wildcard", &["node.invoke"], &["node.invoke.child"]),
+        ("node-no-star-wildcard", &["node.*"], &["node.read"]),
+        ("node-no-operator-implication", &["operator.admin"], &["operator.read"]),
+        ("node-reject-other-prefix", &["other.read"], &["other.read"]),
+        ("node-reject-lookalike-prefix", &["nodes.read"], &["nodes.read"]),
+    ];
+    for (label, baseline, desired) in node_cases {
+        let fixture = Fixture::seeded(label, &["operator.admin"], baseline);
+        let proof = fixture.authorization(CALLER, "operator");
+        fixture.refuse(&proof, json!({"deviceId": TARGET, "role": "node", "scopes": desired}), None, 403);
+    }
+
+    // Publicly approved non-operator tokens still cannot acquire operator management.
+    for role in ["node", "unknown-role"] {
+        let fixture = Fixture::new("non-operator-caller");
+        let granted = format!("{role}.write");
+        fixture.pair(CALLER, &[role], &[&granted]);
+        fixture.pair(TARGET, &["operator", "node"], &["operator.write", "node.invoke"]);
+        fixture.seed_surfaces(CALLER);
+        fixture.seed_surfaces(TARGET);
+        let mut proof = fixture.authorization(CALLER, role);
+        proof.device_id = TARGET.to_owned();
+        proof.role = "operator".to_owned();

+

+        let original = fixture.token(CALLER, role);
+        let before = fixture.observe();

+        fixture.refuse(&proof, json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "scopes": []}), Some("operator.admin"), 401);
+        assert_invalid(&fixture, &original);
+        let captured_before_removal = fixture.authorize_token(&successor);
+        fixture.refuse(&captured_before_removal, json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "scopes": []}), None, 403);
+        let before = fixture.observe();
+        let revoke = fixture.owner().handle_pairing_command(
+            "device.pair.revoke", &json!({"deviceId": CALLER}),
+        ).expect("retire the currently authenticated non-operator role through native whole-device revoke");
+        let retired = fixture.observe();
+        assert_eq!(revoke["revision"].as_u64(), Some(revision(&before) + 1));
+        assert_revision(&retired, revision(&before) + 1);
+        assert_eq!(retired.pending, before.pending);
+        assert_eq!(retired.paired.len(), before.paired.len() - 1);
+        assert_eq!(paired(&retired, TARGET), paired(&before, TARGET));
+        assert!(!retired.paired.iter().any(|row| text(row, "device_id") == CALLER));
+        fixture.refuse(&proof, json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "scopes": []}), Some("operator.admin"), 401);
+        fixture.refuse(&captured_before_removal, json!({"deviceId": CALLER, "scopes": []}), None, 401);
+        assert_invalid(&fixture, &successor);
+    }

+//! DPA-v1: real HTTP ingress, the production pairing owner and durable SQLite.
+//! Contract: projects/openclaw-rust/docs/specs/device-pairing-authenticated-rotation.md.
+//! These adapters contain no authorization policy and do not represent a full App
+//! or physical-device runtime. Executable verification belongs to exact-H Actions.
+
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+use std::fs;
+use std::io::{Read, Write};
+use std::net::{SocketAddr, TcpStream};
+use std::path::PathBuf;
+use std::sync::{
+    Arc, Condvar, Mutex,
+    atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
+    mpsc::{self, Receiver, SyncSender},
+};
+use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};
+use std::time::Duration;
+
+use mahayana_host_runtime::device_pairing_owner::{DevicePairingOwner, DeviceTokenAuthorization};
+use mahayana_host_runtime::gateway_config::GatewayServerConfig;
+use mahayana_host_runtime::gateway_server::{
+    GatewayApi, GatewayCommandContext, GatewayCommandError, GatewayCommandReport,
+    GatewayEventHub, GatewayServer, GatewayServerDeps, start_gateway_server,
+};
+use rusqlite::{Connection, OpenFlags, params, types::Value as SqlValue};
+use serde_json::{Value, json};
+
+const ROTATE: &str = "device.pair.rotateToken";
+const CALLER: &str = "dpa-http-caller";
+const TARGET: &str = "dpa-http-target";
+const NATIVE_TOKEN: &str = "dpa-http-native-secret";
+const WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15);
+const IO_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
+type StoredRow = BTreeMap<String, SqlValue>;
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
+struct StoredState {
+    paired: Vec<StoredRow>,
+    pending: Vec<StoredRow>,
+    revision: Vec<StoredRow>,
+}
+
+fn read_rows(conn: &Connection, sql: &str) -> Vec<StoredRow> {
+    let mut statement = conn.prepare(sql).expect("prepare independent SQL observation");
+    let columns: Vec<_> = statement.column_names().into_iter().map(str::to_owned).collect();
+    statement.query_map([], |row| {
+        columns.iter().enumerate()
+            .map(|(index, name)| Ok((name.clone(), row.get::<_, SqlValue>(index)?)))
+            .collect::<rusqlite::Result<StoredRow>>()
+    }).expect("query durable rows").collect::<rusqlite::Result<Vec<_>>>()
+        .expect("retain complete raw SQL rows")
+}
+
+fn sql_text<'a>(row: &'a StoredRow, column: &str) -> &'a str {
+    match row.get(column) {
+        Some(SqlValue::Text(value)) => value,
+        _ => panic!("expected SQL TEXT in {column}"),
+    }
+}
+
+impl StoredState {
+    fn device(&self, device_id: &str) -> &StoredRow {
+        self.paired.iter().find(|row| sql_text(row, "device_id") == device_id)
+            .expect("observed paired device")
+    }
+
+    fn tokens(&self, device_id: &str) -> Value {
+        serde_json::from_str(sql_text(self.device(device_id), "tokens_json"))
+            .expect("durable role token map")
+    }
+
+    fn token(&self, device_id: &str, role: &str) -> String {
+        self.tokens(device_id)[role]["token"].as_str().expect("issued role token").to_owned()
+    }
+
+    fn revision_number(&self) -> u64 {
+        assert_eq!(self.revision.len(), 1);
+        assert_eq!(sql_text(&self.revision[0], "value_type"), "text");
+        assert_eq!(sql_text(&self.revision[0], "timestamp_type"), "integer");
+        let raw = sql_text(&self.revision[0], "value_json");
+        let value = serde_json::from_str::<String>(raw).expect("quoted decimal revision");
+        let number: u64 = value.parse().expect("unsigned revision");
+        assert_eq!(raw, format!("\"{number}\""));
+        number
+    }
+
+    fn assert_no_secrets_in(&self, reply: &HttpReply) {
+        for row in &self.paired {
+            let tokens: Value = serde_json::from_str(sql_text(row, "tokens_json"))
+                .expect("stored token object");
+            for entry in tokens.as_object().expect("role map").values() {
+                assert!(!reply.raw.contains(entry["token"].as_str().expect("stored token")),
+                    "HTTP reply disclosed a stored credential");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+struct Counts {
+    native: usize,
+    bound: usize,
+    recognized: usize,
+}
+
+#[derive(Default)]
+struct Observations {
+    native: AtomicUsize,
+    bound: AtomicUsize,
+    recognized: AtomicUsize,
+    contexts: Mutex<Vec<(bool, Option<String>)>>,
+    completed: Mutex<Vec<GatewayCommandReport>>,
+}
+
+impl Observations {
+    fn counts(&self) -> Counts {
+        Counts {
+            native: self.native.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
+            bound: self.bound.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
+            recognized: self.recognized.load(Ordering::SeqCst),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// A bounded, releasable barrier: arrival is inside the actual bound hook, after
+// real Gateway authentication. No sleep or scheduling order establishes a race.
+struct HookGate {
+    remaining: AtomicUsize,
+    entered: SyncSender<()>,
+    released: Mutex<bool>,
+    changed: Condvar,
+}
+
+impl HookGate {
+    fn pause(&self) -> Result<(), GatewayCommandError> {
+        if self.remaining.fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |n| n.checked_sub(1)).is_err() {
+            return Ok(());
+        }
+        self.entered.try_send(()).map_err(|_| {
+            GatewayCommandError::Internal("HTTP fixture admission channel unavailable".into())
+        })?;
+        let released = self.released.lock().expect("hook release lock");
+        let (released, _) = self.changed.wait_timeout_while(released, WAIT, |value| !*value)
+            .expect("bounded hook release wait");
+        if !*released {
+            return Err(GatewayCommandError::Internal("HTTP fixture release deadline exceeded".into()));
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+
+    fn release(&self) {
+        *self.released.lock().unwrap_or_else(|error| error.into_inner()) = true;
+        self.changed.notify_all();
+    }
+}
+
+struct GateControl {
+    gate: Arc<HookGate>,
+    entered: Receiver<()>,
+}
+
+impl GateControl {
+    fn wait_for_entries(&self, count: usize) {
+        for _ in 0..count {
+            self.entered.recv_timeout(WAIT).expect("request reached actual bound rotation hook");
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn release(&self) {
+        self.gate.release();
+    }
+}
+
+impl Drop for GateControl {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        self.release();
+    }
+}
+
+struct PairingApi {
+    owner: Option<DevicePairingOwner>,
+    observations: Arc<Observations>,
+    gate: Mutex<Option<Arc<HookGate>>>,
+    closed: SyncSender<()>,
+}
+
+impl PairingApi {
+    fn owner(&self) -> &DevicePairingOwner {
+        self.owner.as_ref().expect("live file-backed owner")
+    }
+}
+
+impl GatewayApi for PairingApi {
+    fn authenticate_device_token(&self, token: &str) -> Result<Option<DeviceTokenAuthorization>, GatewayCommandError> {
+        let authorization = self.owner().authenticate_device_token(token)?;
+        if authorization.is_some() {
+            self.observations.recognized.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        }
+        Ok(authorization)
+    }
+
+    fn call(&self, method: &str, args: Value) -> Result<Value, GatewayCommandError> {
+        self.observations.native.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        self.owner().handle_pairing_command(method, &args)
+    }
+
+    fn rotate_paired_device_token(
+        &self,
+        args: Value,
+        authorization: &DeviceTokenAuthorization,
+        scope_ceiling: Option<&str>,
+        context: &GatewayCommandContext,
+    ) -> Result<Value, GatewayCommandError> {
+        self.observations.bound.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
+        self.observations.contexts.lock().expect("hook context observations")
+            .push((context.authenticated, context.request_id.clone()));
+        let gate = self.gate.lock().expect("optional hook barrier").clone();
+        if let Some(gate) = gate {
+            gate.pause()?;
+        }
+        self.owner().rotate_token_for_authenticated_device(&args, authorization, scope_ceiling)
+    }
+
+    fn on_command_complete(&self, report: GatewayCommandReport) {
+        self.observations.completed.lock().expect("command reports").push(report);
+    }
+}
+
+impl Drop for PairingApi {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        // A listener close alone does not join its detached connection threads.
+        // Acknowledge only after their final API reference and SQLite owner close.
+        drop(self.owner.take());
+        let _ = self.closed.try_send(());
+    }
+}
+
+struct LegacyApi(Arc<PairingApi>);
+
+impl GatewayApi for LegacyApi {
+    fn call(&self, method: &str, args: Value) -> Result<Value, GatewayCommandError> {
+        self.0.call(method, args)
+    }
+
+    fn authenticate_device_token(&self, token: &str) -> Result<Option<DeviceTokenAuthorization>, GatewayCommandError> {
+        self.0.authenticate_device_token(token)
+    }
+
+    fn on_command_complete(&self, report: GatewayCommandReport) {
+        self.0.on_command_complete(report);
+    }
+    // Deliberately inherit GatewayApi's default bound rotation implementation.
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug)]
+struct HttpReply {
+    status: u16,
+    body: Value,
+    raw: String,
+}
+
+fn post_to_port(port: u16, method: &str, body: &str, authorization: Option<&str>, headers: &str) -> Result<HttpReply, String> {
+    let address = SocketAddr::from(([127, 0, 0, 1], port));
+    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect_timeout(&address, IO_WAIT).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(IO_WAIT)).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(IO_WAIT)).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    let authorization = authorization.map(|value| format!("Authorization: {value}\r\n")).unwrap_or_default();
+    let request = format!(
+        "POST /api/{method} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1\r\n{authorization}{headers}Content-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}",
+        body.len(),
+    );
+    stream.write_all(request.as_bytes()).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    stream.flush().map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    let mut raw = String::new();
+    stream.read_to_string(&mut raw).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    let status = raw.lines().next().and_then(|line| line.split_whitespace().nth(1))
+        .ok_or("missing HTTP status")?.parse::<u16>().map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    let body = serde_json::from_str(raw.split_once("\r\n\r\n").ok_or("missing HTTP body")?.1)
+        .map_err(|error| format!("non-JSON HTTP body: {error}"))?;
+    Ok(HttpReply { status, body, raw })
+}
+
+struct PendingHttp {
+    result: Receiver<Result<HttpReply, String>>,
+    thread: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
+    gate: Arc<HookGate>,
+}
+
+impl PendingHttp {
+    fn finish(mut self) -> HttpReply {
+        let result = self.result.recv_timeout(IO_WAIT).expect("bounded HTTP completion");
+        self.thread.take().expect("owned HTTP client").join().expect("HTTP client completed");
+        result.expect("actual HTTP transport")
+    }
+}
+
+impl Drop for PendingHttp {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        if self.thread.is_some() {
+            self.gate.release();
+            // Panic cleanup releases the hook before joining the exact client.
+            // A deadline never becomes an unbounded join or successful evidence.
+            if self.result.recv_timeout(IO_WAIT).is_ok() {
+                let _ = self.thread.take().expect("owned client").join();
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+struct PairingGateway {
+    server: Option<GatewayServer>,
+    api: Option<Arc<PairingApi>>,
+    closed: Option<Receiver<()>>,
+    gate: Option<Arc<HookGate>>,
+    observations: Arc<Observations>,
+    config: GatewayServerConfig,
+    legacy: bool,
+    shutdown_failed: bool,
+    root: PathBuf,
+    db_path: PathBuf,
+}
+
+impl PairingGateway {
+    fn new(configured: bool, host: &str, legacy: bool) -> Self {
+        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("fabushi-dpa-http-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4()));
+        fs::create_dir(&root).expect("exclusively create owned HTTP fixture directory");
+        let mut fixture = Self {
+            server: None, api: None, closed: None, gate: None,
+            observations: Arc::new(Observations::default()),
+            config: GatewayServerConfig {
+                host: host.into(), port: None,
+                auth_token: configured.then(|| NATIVE_TOKEN.into()), tls: None,
+            },
+            legacy, shutdown_failed: false, db_path: root.join("pairing.sqlite"), root,
+        };
+        fixture.open();
+        fixture
+    }
+
+    fn seeded(role: &str, scopes: &[&str]) -> Self {
+        let fixture = Self::new(false, "127.0.0.1", false);
+        fixture.seed(role, scopes);
+        fixture
+    }
+
+    fn open(&mut self) {
+        let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::sync_channel(1);
+        let api = Arc::new(PairingApi {
+            owner: Some(DevicePairingOwner::new(&self.db_path).expect("open actual durable pairing owner")),
+            observations: Arc::clone(&self.observations), gate: Mutex::new(None), closed: sender,
+        });
+        let dispatch: Arc<dyn GatewayApi> = if self.legacy {
+            Arc::new(LegacyApi(Arc::clone(&api)))
+        } else {
+            api.clone()
+        };
+        self.server = Some(start_gateway_server(GatewayServerDeps {
+            api: dispatch, events: GatewayEventHub::default(), local_exec: None, webauthn: None,
+            config: self.config.clone(), started_at: 1,
+        }).expect("start real TCP Gateway"));
+        self.api = Some(api);
+        self.closed = Some(receiver);
+    }
+
+    fn stop(&mut self) -> bool {
+        if let Some(gate) = self.gate.take() {
+            gate.release();
+        }
+        if let Some(server) = self.server.take() {
+            server.close();
+        }
+        drop(self.api.take());
+        if let Some(closed) = self.closed.take() {
+            self.shutdown_failed |= closed.recv_timeout(IO_WAIT).is_err();
+        }
+        // Keep a failed shutdown terminal: a later Drop must not mistake a
+        // consumed timeout receiver for proof that an old owner has closed.
+        !self.shutdown_failed
+    }
+
+    fn reopen(&mut self) {
+        assert!(self.stop(), "all owned connection references and SQLite owner must close before reopen");
+        self.open();
+    }
+
+    fn owner(&self) -> &DevicePairingOwner {
+        self.api.as_ref().expect("live adapter").owner()
+    }
+
+    fn observe(&self) -> StoredState {
+        let mut conn = Connection::open_with_flags(&self.db_path, OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY)
+            .expect("independent read-only SQLite observer");
+        let tx = conn.transaction().expect("consistent read-only snapshot");
+        let state = StoredState {
+            paired: read_rows(&tx, "SELECT * FROM device_pairing_paired ORDER BY device_id"),
+            pending: read_rows(&tx, "SELECT * FROM device_pairing_pending ORDER BY request_id"),
+            revision: read_rows(&tx,
+                "SELECT state_key, typeof(value_json) AS value_type, value_json,
+                        typeof(updated_at_ms) AS timestamp_type, updated_at_ms
+                 FROM config_machine_state WHERE state_key = 'devicePairing.revision'"),
+        };
+        tx.commit().expect("finish read-only snapshot");
+        conn.close().expect("close observer before mutation or reopen");
+        state
+    }
+
+    fn approve(&self, device_id: &str, roles: &[&str], scopes: &[&str]) {
+        let request = self.owner().handle_pair_request(&json!({
+            "deviceId": device_id, "publicKey": format!("dpa-key-{device_id}"),
+            "role": roles[0], "roles": roles, "scopes": scopes,
+            "displayName": format!("DPA {device_id}"), "platform": "linux",
+        })).expect("real pending pairing");
+        self.owner().handle_pair_approve(&json!({"requestId": request["requestId"]}))
+            .expect("production approval issues actual credentials");
+    }
+
+    fn seed(&self, role: &str, scopes: &[&str]) {
+        let mut caller_scopes = scopes.to_vec();
+        let caller_roles = if role == "operator" {
+            caller_scopes.push("node.invoke");
+            vec!["operator", "node"]
+        } else {
+            vec![role]
+        };
+        self.approve(CALLER, &caller_roles, &caller_scopes);
+        self.approve(TARGET, &["operator", "node"], &["operator.read", "operator.write", "node.invoke"]);
+        for device_id in [CALLER, TARGET] {
+            self.owner().handle_pair_request(&json!({
+                "deviceId": device_id, "publicKey": format!("dpa-repair-{device_id}"),
+                "roles": ["operator", "node"], "scopes": ["operator.read", "node.invoke"],
+            })).expect("fresh pending repair remains independently observable");
+        }
+        let conn = Connection::open_with_flags(&self.db_path, OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_WRITE)
+            .expect("explicit fixture-only retained-surface writer");
+        for device_id in [CALLER, TARGET] {
+            assert_eq!(conn.execute(
+                "UPDATE device_pairing_paired SET node_surface_json = ?1, pending_node_surface_json = ?2
+                 WHERE device_id = ?3",
+                params!["{\"generation\":7,\"commands\":[\"system.run\"]}",
+                    "{\"generation\":8,\"commands\":[\"system.notify\"]}", device_id],
+            ).expect("seed retained and pending node surfaces"), 1);
+        }
+        conn.close().expect("close fixture writer");
+        let state = self.observe();
+        assert_eq!(state.paired.len(), 2);
+        assert_eq!(state.pending.len(), 2);
+        assert_eq!(state.revision_number(), 2);
+        self.assert_all_current_tokens(&state);
+    }
+
+    fn assert_authorized(&self, token: &str, device_id: &str, role: &str, scopes: &Value) {
+        let authorization = self.owner().authenticate_device_token(token)
+            .expect("production token lookup").expect("current credential recognized");
+        assert_eq!(authorization.device_id, device_id);
+        assert_eq!(authorization.role, role);
+        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(authorization.scopes).expect("scope projection"), *scopes);
+    }
+
+    fn assert_retired(&self, token: &str) {
+        assert!(self.owner().authenticate_device_token(token).expect("retired credential lookup").is_none());
+    }
+
+    fn assert_all_current_tokens(&self, state: &StoredState) {
+        for row in &state.paired {
+            let device_id = sql_text(row, "device_id");
+            for (role, entry) in state.tokens(device_id).as_object().expect("role tokens") {
+                self.assert_authorized(entry["token"].as_str().expect("token"), device_id, role, &entry["scopes"]);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn post(&self, method: &str, body: &str, authorization: Option<&str>, headers: &str) -> HttpReply {
+        post_to_port(self.server.as_ref().expect("owned server").port(), method, body, authorization, headers)
+            .expect("real TCP HTTP response")
+    }
+
+    fn rotate(&self, args: &Value, token: &str, headers: &str) -> HttpReply {
+        self.post(ROTATE, &args.to_string(), Some(&format!("Bearer {token}")), headers)
+    }
+
+    fn deny(&self, body: &str, authorization: Option<&str>, headers: &str, status: u16, bound: Option<usize>, recognized: usize) -> HttpReply {
+        let before = self.observe();
+        let counts = self.observations.counts();
+        let reply = self.post(ROTATE, body, authorization, headers);
+        assert_refused(&reply, status, &before);
+        assert_eq!(self.observe(), before, "refusal preserves every caller/target/pending/revision SQL value");
+        let after = self.observations.counts();
+        assert_eq!(after.native, counts.native, "paired or invalid credentials must never fall back to native call");
+        assert_eq!(after.recognized, counts.recognized + recognized);
+        if let Some(bound) = bound {
+            assert_eq!(after.bound, counts.bound + bound);
+        } else {
+            assert!((counts.bound..=counts.bound + 1).contains(&after.bound), "at most one bound dispatch");
+        }
+        self.assert_all_current_tokens(&before);
+        reply
+    }
+
+    fn assert_rotation(&self, before: &StoredState, reply: &HttpReply, device_id: &str, role: &str, delivery: &str, scopes: &[&str]) -> String {
+        assert_eq!(reply.status, 200, "{}", reply.raw);
+        assert_eq!(reply.body["deviceId"], device_id);
+        assert_eq!(reply.body["role"], role);
+        assert_eq!(reply.body["tokenDelivery"], delivery);
+        assert!(reply.body["rotatedAtMs"].as_i64().is_some());
+        let after = self.observe();
+        assert_eq!(after.revision_number(), before.revision_number() + 1, "one committed replacement");
+        assert_eq!(reply.body["revision"].as_u64(), Some(after.revision_number()));
+        assert_eq!(after.pending, before.pending, "rotation preserves pending pairing rows");
+        assert_eq!(after.paired.len(), before.paired.len());
+        for old_row in &before.paired {
+            let id = sql_text(old_row, "device_id");
+            if id != device_id {
+                assert_eq!(after.device(id), old_row, "unaddressed device remains byte-for-byte intact");
+            }
+        }
+        let mut identity_before = before.device(device_id).clone();
+        let mut identity_after = after.device(device_id).clone();
+        for column in ["tokens_json", "node_surface_json", "pending_node_surface_json"] {
+            identity_before.remove(column);
+            identity_after.remove(column);
+        }
+        assert_eq!(identity_after, identity_before, "roles, approval baseline, identity and timestamps remain intact");
+        for column in ["node_surface_json", "pending_node_surface_json"] {
+            assert_eq!(after.device(device_id).get(column), Some(&SqlValue::Null));
+        }
+        let old_tokens = before.tokens(device_id);
+        let new_tokens = after.tokens(device_id);
+        assert_eq!(new_tokens.as_object().expect("new token map").len(), old_tokens.as_object().expect("old token map").len());
+        for (other_role, entry) in old_tokens.as_object().expect("old token map") {
+            if other_role != role {
+                assert_eq!(&new_tokens[other_role], entry, "nonselected role token and metadata remain intact");
+            }
+        }
+        let token = after.token(device_id, role);
+        assert!(token.starts_with("sand-device-tok-"));
+        assert_ne!(token, before.token(device_id, role));
+        assert_eq!(new_tokens[role]["role"], role);
+        assert_eq!(new_tokens[role]["scopes"], json!(scopes));
+        assert_eq!(new_tokens[role]["rotatedAtMs"], reply.body["rotatedAtMs"]);
+        before.assert_no_secrets_in(reply);
+        if delivery == "in-band" {
+            assert_eq!(reply.body["token"].as_str(), Some(token.as_str()));
+        } else {
+            assert!(reply.body.get("token").is_none());
+            after.assert_no_secrets_in(reply);
+        }
+        self.assert_retired(&before.token(device_id, role));
+        self.assert_all_current_tokens(&after);
+        token
+    }
+
+    fn install_gate(&mut self, count: usize) -> GateControl {
+        let (sender, entered) = mpsc::sync_channel(count);
+        let gate = Arc::new(HookGate {
+            remaining: AtomicUsize::new(count), entered: sender,
+            released: Mutex::new(false), changed: Condvar::new(),
+        });
+        *self.api.as_ref().expect("adapter").gate.lock().expect("install hook barrier") = Some(Arc::clone(&gate));
+        self.gate = Some(Arc::clone(&gate));
+        GateControl { gate, entered }
+    }
+
+    fn spawn_rotation(&self, gate: &GateControl, args: Value, token: &str) -> PendingHttp {
+        let port = self.server.as_ref().expect("owned server").port();
+        let body = args.to_string();
+        let bearer = format!("Bearer {token}");
+        let (sender, result) = mpsc::sync_channel(1);
+        let handle = thread::spawn(move || {
+            let reply = post_to_port(port, ROTATE, &body, Some(&bearer), "");
+            let _ = sender.send(reply);
+        });
+        PendingHttp { result, thread: Some(handle), gate: Arc::clone(&gate.gate) }
+    }
+}

+impl Drop for PairingGateway {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        if self.stop() {
+            let result = fs::remove_dir_all(&self.root);
+            if !thread::panicking() {
+                result.expect("remove only the closed owned HTTP fixture directory");
+            }
+        } else {
+            eprintln!("DPA fixture retained because owner shutdown was not acknowledged: {}", self.root.display());
+            assert!(thread::panicking(), "bounded owned Gateway shutdown failed");
+        }
+    }
+}

+fn assert_refused(reply: &HttpReply, status: u16, state: &StoredState) {
+    assert_eq!(reply.status, status, "{}", reply.raw);

+    assert!(reply.body.get("token").is_none());
+    assert!(reply.body.get("revision").is_none(), "a refusal cannot acknowledge a mutation");
+    state.assert_no_secrets_in(reply);

## Finding DPA-R1-SEC-01 — P2: DPA receipt can claim success after capture has failed

**Location:** `.github/workflows/rust-desktop-runtime.yml`, the inline receipt builder in `Require Memory, device pairing, roster search and palette positives from scoped macOS commands`; specifically the new DPA case construction and `rotation_accepted` at candidate lines 1482–1509. The adjacent producer is `run_recovery_check` at lines 593–607, and `project-log.py`'s terminal capture refusal is at lines 469–474 and 570–589.

**Concrete failure scenario:** Both new Cargo test commands complete with all required positive names and the expected summaries (9/0/0 and 8/0/0), and their entries in `command-exit-codes.tsv` are zero. The bounded `project-log.py` projection nevertheless fails, for example because the evidence budget is exhausted or because the existing `projection-refused.json` terminal latch was set during an earlier command. `run_recovery_check` correctly records a nonzero capture status (86) in `capture-exit-codes.tsv` and returns failure. The following receipt step deliberately runs after either success or failure of `ocrm_recovery`, but the new DPA code reads only `command-exit-codes.tsv`. If the node-binding positive is present, both `oracle_accepted` values and `rotation_accepted` still become true, and `device-pairing-rotation.receipt.json` is written with `"result": "passed"` despite the failed capture.

**Why this is a defect:** The DPA implementation contract explicitly requires receipts with zero command **and capture** exits. The new per-contract receipt omits both the capture result and its acceptance predicate. It can therefore publish an internally misleading positive artifact precisely when the existing wrapper has declared its evidence capture incomplete. The enclosing recovery step/job remains failed; this finding does **not** claim that the entire workflow becomes green or that this opens runtime authorization.

**Minimal fix:** For each of the two DPA labels, read the matching capture records, include them in the execution receipt, and require exactly one `[label, "0"]` capture record in addition to the existing command-exit, name, and summary predicates. Missing, duplicate, nonzero, or unreadable capture evidence must prevent `oracle_accepted`. Bind the reused node-binding result to its corresponding command/capture evidence as appropriate rather than relying on the positive name alone. Preserve the existing wrapper's sticky refusal and continue to distinguish a captured Cargo success from a complete evidence success. A focused Actions instrument control can feed otherwise successful 9/8 logs with one failed or missing capture record and require a non-passing DPA receipt; no product runtime change is needed.

**Location:** `.github/workflows/rust-desktop-runtime.yml:1482–1504`, specifically the `rotation_cases` `oracle_accepted` expression at 1497–1498. Its cases pin literal scope outcomes rather than copying `role_scope_allows`. They cover foreign/same-file foreign issuer proofs, altered public projections, literal/implied/prefix scope distinctions, header/body forgery, omitted/empty/narrow desired scopes, live/approval changes, corrupt types/JSON/baselines, revision corruption/exhaustion and controlled repair, replacement/removal/reopen, and non-operator management denial. The test's explicit writer helpers are fixture fault injection; they do not become a product authorization implementation.

The HTTP fixture calls `start_gateway_server` and real TCP/HTTP, delegates directly to the production owner, and records native/bound/authentication counts plus successful command reports. It proves default-hook refusal, no native fallback for explicit failed credentials, configured native secret/credential-absent native/public controls, cross-device denial before target observation, admin/non-operator/scope ceilings, identity-derived disclosure and reopen. The hook barrier is after real authentication and before production mutation. It deterministically admits both concurrent original credentials, then releases them and requires exactly one 200, one 401 and one revision advance. Retirement cases compare against the independently observed state **after** replacement/removal; unchanged and unrelated-role controls make the refusal oracle causal.

Barrier waits, HTTP I/O waits and owner-close acknowledgements are bounded. Cleanup releases only the fixture's gate, joins only its client when completion is observed, closes its own server/API owner, and removes only its unique directory after acknowledged owner closure. A consumed shutdown timeout stays terminal, preserving the fixture rather than falsely treating it as closed. Listener shutdown uses the existing implementation; connection-thread ownership is accounted for by final API/owner destruction acknowledgement. These tests do not run the full shipping App, and their comments and receipt scope acknowledge that limit.

### 1. The former equality assertion conflicts with the DPA proof contract

The DPA shared Rust contract explicitly distinguishes persisted tokens from newly issued proofs after reopen. `DeviceTokenAuthorization` derives `PartialEq`/`Eq` over its public projection and private proof. The proof's explicit equality implementation requires `Arc::ptr_eq` on its issuer, plus device ID, role, token fingerprint, and admitted scopes (`source/host/src/device_pairing_owner.rs:15–60`). Both file-backed and in-memory owner construction allocate a new issuer (`305–330`). Authentication constructs a proof by cloning that owner's issuer after the actual locked bearer comparison, and seals the same principal, role, SHA-256 fingerprint, and scopes that correspond to the accepted credential (`468–536`).

The channel fixture really constructs a new `CredentialApi` and `DevicePairingOwner` over the same SQLite path when it reopens (`channel_gateway_authorization_contract.rs:76–85, 231–240`). The retained original credential continues to own its original proof's `Arc`; consequently, the original allocation remains alive. Allocation identity cannot accidentally become equal through reuse of a freed original issuer while that credential is retained. The final authentication therefore returns the same durable public identity/grants with a different issuer allocation.

The relevant production semantics are explicit:

1. `DeviceTokenAuthorization` derives equality over all three public fields **and** its private proof (`source/host/src/device_pairing_owner.rs:21–27`).
2. `DeviceTokenProof::eq` requires `Arc::ptr_eq` of the issuer, sealed device/role, token SHA-256, and admitted scopes (`47–57`). A freshly opened file-backed owner creates a new `Arc<()>` issuer (`306–318`).

Consequently, the final old full equality demanded something DPA explicitly forbids: the same owner-issued proof across owner reopen. The new code requires successful authentication of the exact original token, exact equality of device ID/role/scopes, and inequality of the complete sealed authorization. Given the authentication constructor, the public equality checks also pin the corresponding sealed projection, and the unchanged token input pins the fingerprint; the intentionally different issuer explains the inequality. The private proof stays private, and failure diagnostics continue to use its redacted Debug implementation.

The change does not collapse success to merely “Some authorization,” ignore a grant, normalize away scope order, synthesize a credential, or replace production authentication.
